Three steps from unboxing to a live display. You need a Raspberry Pi 5 (4 GB+), a microSD card and an HDMI screen.
Download the PitchTribe OS image and flash it with Raspberry Pi Imager. It bundles Raspberry Pi OS Lite, the PitchTribe stack and kiosk mode.
Plug the Pi 5 into any HDMI display and power it on. PitchTribe boots straight into full-screen kiosk mode — no keyboard or mouse needed.
Open the dashboard on any phone, tablet or laptop on your club network. Update notices, menus and fixtures live — from the bar, the car park, wherever.

The software is. PitchTribe is MIT-licensed open source, with no subscriptions, per-screen licences or hidden fees. You pay for the hardware once, and for the electricity it uses — a Pi 5 draws a few watts, though the TV it drives will be the larger share.
Does it need an internet connection?
No. Displays and the dashboard work entirely over your local network. Internet is only needed for optional features like league fixture imports and software updates.
Can I run more than one screen?
Yes. Each Pi 5 drives up to two displays, and you can add as many Pis as you like — manage them all from one dashboard, each showing its own playlist.

The parts list is honest about the parts. These are the things that actually hold up an installation on the day, roughly in the order they bite.
The official case has no VESA pattern, so you want a bracket or plate — otherwise the Pi ends up cable-tied behind the TV. Per screen.
A mains socket near the screen
The official power lead is 1.5 m. Wall brackets are rarely next to a double socket, and this is the single most common reason an install stalls halfway.
Somewhere for the network lead to go
A 15 m lead assumes a spare port at the other end, and a route to get there. Wi-Fi avoids the problem entirely if the signal reaches.
Not in that total. If a screen has to be bought it will dwarf everything above it, and the TV is also where nearly all the running electricity goes — not the Pi.
Cards are the usual failure on an always-on Pi, and a dead one at 2pm on a Saturday is the version of that you will meet. A second imaged card is cheap insurance.
